propositions: Negative caplog assertions (assert not [...]) pass vacuously when zero records arrive, masking 100% loss of coverage and rendering the test effectively inert.
Logger propagation disabled globally and never restored in production code poisons downstream tests' caplog capture, making their assertions void while appearing green.
Logger level raised to WARNING globally and never restored silently drops INFO-level records at the originating logger, evading caplog.at_level(INFO) which only raises the root level.
Test run order determines whether a caplog assertion is live or void, causing the same assertion and commit to pass or fail non-deterministically depending on worker distribution.

Five negative caplog assertions across the suite are reachable but exposed to silent coverage loss from these two poisoning vectors; positive assertions fail loudly when void, masking the class of silent failures.

An autouse fixture with instrumentation must detect and fail loudly when logger propagation is disabled or logger level is raised, catching the poisoning at its source rather than at random downstream victims.
